title: Tower orientation and tower purity isomorphism
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$ with algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Derived categories, their shifts and derived tensor products are as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-derived-tensor]. Use the coefficient tower categories and their normalized constructible subcategories [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], with finite constructible finite-Tor objects defined in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Let $F_\bullet=Rf_{!,\bullet}\dashv G_\bullet=f^!_\bullet$ be the adjunction of [det-sp-tower-gluing], with its finite-level units and counits. Let $f^*_\bullet$ denote finite-coefficient derived pullback level by level [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and use the Tate twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], levelwise on towers. Put $\omega_{f,\bullet}=G_\bullet(\mathcal O_{E,Y}/\ell^\bullet)$.

(1) The diagonal construction of [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] gives an orientation
$$a_\bullet:(\mathcal O_{E,X}/\ell^\bullet)(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{f,\bullet}$$
in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(X,\mathcal O_E))$, whose level $n\geq1$ is the finite orientation with coefficients $\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$ (the inverse of the finite diagonal isomorphism $\omega_{f,n}\simeq(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_X(d)[2d]$).

(2) For $K_\bullet\in\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$, let $t_{K_\bullet}:f^*_\bullet K_\bullet\otimes^L\omega_{f,\bullet}\to G_\bullet K_\bullet$ be the adjoint transpose, under $F_\bullet\dashv G_\bullet$, of the projection-formula composite
$$F_\bullet(f^*_\bullet K_\bullet\otimes^L\omega_{f,\bullet})\simeq K_\bullet\otimes^L F_\bullet\omega_{f,\bullet}\xrightarrow{1\otimes\varepsilon^\bullet}K_\bullet,$$
where the tensor and projection-formula notation is as in [def-exchange-projection]. The composite
$$\gamma_{f,\bullet}(K_\bullet):f^*_\bullet K_\bullet(d)[2d]\simeq f^*_\bullet K_\bullet\otimes^L(\mathcal O_{E,X}/\ell^\bullet)(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{1\otimes a_\bullet}f^*_\bullet K_\bullet\otimes^L\omega_{f,\bullet}\xrightarrow{t_{K_\bullet}}G_\bullet K_\bullet$$
is an isomorphism, natural in $K_\bullet\in\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$, in $\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$. Its level $n$ is the finite purity comparison $\gamma_{f,\mathcal O_E/\ell^n}(K_n)$ of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map].

(3) Both $F_\bullet$ and $G_\bullet$ preserve normalized constructible towers.

source.place: Statement clauses (1)-(3), id det-sp-tower-gamma; clause (2) orientation direction corrected to match the displayed source and target; surrounding unit sk-prop-sp-tower-geometric

proof.text: Write $R_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$. If $\ell=u\varpi_E^e$ with $u$ a unit, then $(\ell^n)=(\varpi_E^{en})$, so $R_n=A_{E,en}$: every finite purity statement applies at index $en$, including when $E$ is ramified. Let $a_n:R_{n,X}(d)[2d]\to f_{R_n}^!R_{n,Y}$ be the inverse of the finite diagonal isomorphism [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object]. Equivalently $a_n=\gamma_{f,R_n}(R_{n,Y})$: by [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] the latter is the inverse orientation followed by the tensor map at the tensor unit. By [def-pur-co-smoothness] this tensor map is the transpose of the counit $Rf_{!,R_n}\omega_{f,n}\to R_{n,Y}$, hence is $1_{\omega_{f,n}}$ by the adjunction triangle identity. Here the projection map with coefficient-unit second input is the identity under the unit identifications: in the defining formula of [def-exchange-projection], its proper factor is $Rp_*(\varepsilon_p)\circ\eta_p=1$ and its open-immersion factor is the tensor-unit identification. Thus this construction uses exactly the diagonal/DNC normalization, with orientation pointing from twist to dualizing object.

source.place: (1), identify the finite orientations; (2), tensor map at the coefficient unit

proof.text: For $n\geq m$, apply [det-sp-reduction-compatibilities](3) to $R_n\twoheadrightarrow R_m$ and $K=R_{n,Y}$. The purity maps in that clause are those of [det-sp-finite-general-ring](3), built from the orientation of its clause (1); by its clause (2) that orientation agrees with the one obtained by running the diagonal construction directly with $R_n=A_{E,en}$-coefficients, i.e. with the finite diagonal isomorphism of [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] at index $en$, and its tensor map is the transpose $\theta$ of step 1. Hence its $\gamma_{f,R_n}(R_{n,Y})$ is $a_n$ of step 1, and likewise at $R_m$. The clause therefore gives $c_{n,m}(R_{n,Y})\circ(a_n)_{R_m}=a_m$ under the canonical twist reduction. These twist reductions are ordinary reductions of rank-one locally free sheaves by [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor](3). By [det-sp-tower-gluing](3), the reduction maps of $\omega_{f,\bullet}=G_\bullet R_{\bullet,Y}$ are precisely $c_{n,m}(R_{n,Y})$, since the coefficient-unit reduction maps are identities. This is the required compatibility of the finite orientations with the actual transitions of the tower, and does not infer coefficient compatibility from uniqueness for a fixed coefficient ring.

source.place: (1), coefficient compatibility of the diagonal orientations

proof.text: We construct a morphism in the derived category of strict towers, rather than assuming that a compatible family of arbitrary derived morphisms lifts. By the chart formula of [det-sp-tower-gluing](1), $\omega_{f,\bullet}[-2d]$ has cohomology only in degree zero. Alternatively its evaluations do, by step 1; exact, jointly conservative evaluation in the abelian tower category [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian] detects the vanishing of each other cohomology sheaf. Put $W_\bullet=H^0(\omega_{f,\bullet}[-2d])$. By [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single] at degree zero, $W_\bullet[0]\simeq\omega_{f,\bullet}[-2d]$. At each level, $a_n[-2d]$ is a unique map of sheaves $R_{n,X}(d)\to W_n$ by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful]. Write $\alpha_n:R_{n,X}(d)\to W_n$ for these sheaf isomorphisms, $q_{n,m}$ for the Tate quotient transition, and $t^W_{n,m}$ for the transition of $W_\bullet$. By [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian](3), the reduction map of $W_\bullet[0]$ is induced by $t^W_{n,m}$. Each $W_n$ is locally free of rank one via $\alpha_n$, so its derived reduction is its ordinary tensor reduction by [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor](3). Consequently step 2, after removing the shift and using full faithfulness, reads $t^W_{n,m}\circ\alpha_n=\alpha_m\circ q_{n,m}$ as an equality of semilinear sheaf maps. Multiplying this equality by the two inverses gives $\alpha_m^{-1}\circ t^W_{n,m}=q_{n,m}\circ\alpha_n^{-1}$. By [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers] they therefore define an actual map of tower sheaves $R_{\bullet,X}(d)\to W_\bullet$. Its inverse family also commutes with transitions, so it is an isomorphism of tower sheaves. Shifting by $[2d]$ gives $a_\bullet$ in clause (1), with exactly the prescribed finite levels.

source.place: (1), rank-one tower sheaves after removing the common shift

proof.text: Choose common Tor bounds $[a,b]$ for $K_\bullet$. At every level $R_n=A_{E,en}$, [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] applies to the separated finite-type morphism $f$ and the bounded constructible finite-Tor complex $K_n$. It gives constructible $f_{R_n}^*K_n$ with Tor interval $[a,b]$. The interval is independent of $n$, since the cited assertion preserves the specified interval, not just existence of some finite interval.

source.place: (2), domain of the transpose: finite pullback preservation

proof.text: By [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free](3)-(4) and [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], $R_{n,X}(d)$ is a constructible locally free line: the unit if $d=0$, and a tensor power of the Tate line if $d>0$. Locally trivializing this line identifies tensoring with it with the identity, so it preserves the Tor interval $[a,b]$ and constructibility. Shifting by $[2d]$ changes the interval to $[a-2d,b-2d]$; testing the Tor bound on the coefficient unit gives the same cohomological bound. Thus $P_\bullet=f^*_\bullet K_\bullet(d)[2d]$ lies in the uniform constructible finite-Tor tower category [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]. Step 3 identifies $Q_\bullet=f^*_\bullet K_\bullet\otimes^L\omega_{f,\bullet}$ with $P_\bullet$, so $Q_\bullet$ is also in the tower adjunction domain.

source.place: (2), domain of the transpose: Tate line and uniform shifted bounds

proof.text: The finite-etale-origin hypotheses of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](2a) hold. A field is Noetherian because its only ideals are zero and the whole field. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $X,Y$ are Noetherian, hence quasi-compact, and [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] makes them quasi-separated. Every $R_n$ is a finite, hence Noetherian, ring. The equivalence of [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] therefore supplies a bounded constructible finite-Tor etale-origin witness for each intrinsic finite-Tor level of $K_\bullet$ and of $\omega_{f,\bullet}$ (the latter is a shifted Tate line by step 1). Steps 3 and 5 give common lower cohomological bounds. These are precisely the two input towers required for the projection formula; compatible choices of the witnesses are not required.

source.place: (2), hypotheses of the tower projection formula: qcqs and etale-origin witnesses

proof.text: Use [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](2a) to form the tower projection-formula/counit composite $h:F_\bullet Q_\bullet\to K_\bullet$ displayed in the statement. The adjunction of [det-sp-tower-gluing] defines its transpose $t=G_\bullet(h)\circ\eta_\bullet(Q_\bullet)$. By clause (3) of that node, evaluation carries $G_\bullet$, its unit and its counit to the finite ones; the projection map evaluates to the finite projection map by [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](2a). Hence $t_n=f^!_{R_n}(h_n)\circ\eta_{R_n}(Q_n)=\theta_{f,K_n}$, the specified transpose in [def-pur-co-smoothness]. Composing $t$ with $1\otimes a_\bullet$ and twist reassociation constructs an actual tower map $\gamma_{f,\bullet}(K_\bullet)$ whose level is exactly the map of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map]. Naturality follows from the natural adjunction bijection applied to the natural projection-formula/counit composite, then composition with the fixed orientation and natural twist reassociation. This constructs the map before testing its evaluations.

source.place: (2), tower transpose, finite evaluation formula and naturality

proof.text: Every level of the map in step 7 is an isomorphism by [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity], applied at index $en$. The source category membership and the common shifted Tor and cohomological bounds were verified before the transpose in steps 4-5. The target is in the same tower category by [det-sp-tower-gluing]. The level conservativity of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](3) now makes the already constructed map an isomorphism in the ambient tower derived category, and hence in the full subcategory $\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$ of [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]: both its source and target have constructible levels and cohomological and Tor amplitude bounds independent of the level. No reduction-isomorphism condition is needed for this subcategory. This proves every assertion of clause (2); preservation of the normalized subcategory is proved in steps 9-10.

source.place: (2), levelwise isomorphy and membership in the uniform bounded category

proof.text:
Let $C_\bullet$ be normalized and write $\rho^C_{n,m}:(C_n)_{R_m}\to C_m$ for its reduction isomorphisms. The reduction map of $F_\bullet C_\bullet$ is
$$\rho^{FC}_{n,m}=Rf_{!,R_m}(\rho^C_{n,m})\circ b_{R_n,R_m}(C_n).$$
Indeed, evaluation of $Rp_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}$ is the finite compactification composite by [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](1); its coefficient reduction is first the coefficient exchange for $Rp_*$ and the extension-by-zero tensor identification, followed by the image of $\rho^C_{n,m}$. This is precisely the defining compactification normalization of $b$ in [det-sp-reduction-direct-image]. Both factors of the displayed map are isomorphisms, the first because a functor preserves inverses and the second by that cited theorem. No flatness of $R_m$ over $R_n$ is assumed. For common input Tor bounds $[a,b]$, [det-sp-tower-bound-uniform] gives common output bounds $[a,b+2d]$ and levelwise constructibility, because the smooth morphism has all geometric fibres of dimension $d$. Thus the levelwise constructibility, level-independent cohomological and Tor amplitude bounds, and reduction-isomorphism condition in the current definition [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers] hold for $F_\bullet C_\bullet$.

Let $K_\bullet$ be normalized and put $P_\bullet=f^*_\bullet K_\bullet(d)[2d]$. Its reduction maps are $f_{R_m}^*(\rho^K_{n,m})(d)[2d]$ under the canonical coefficient identifications: pullback commutes with derived coefficient extension by [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], the twist reduction is [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor](3), and shifts commute termwise. These maps are isomorphisms; the common bounds and constructibility were checked in steps 4-5. For $G_\bullet K_\bullet$, [det-sp-tower-gluing](3) gives
$$\rho^{GK}_{n,m}=f_{R_m}^!(\rho^K_{n,m})\circ c_{n,m}(K_n).$$
By [det-sp-reduction-compatibilities](3), whose purity maps are, by [det-sp-finite-general-ring](2)-(3) as in step 2, the maps $\gamma_{f,R}$ of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] used in steps 7-8, followed by naturality in $K$ of $\gamma_{f,R_m}$ ([det-sp-finite-general-ring](3); equivalently the argument of the last sentence of step 7 at one level), applied to $\rho^K_{n,m}:(K_n)_{R_m}\to K_m$, where $(K_n)_{R_m}\in\Dctf$ by [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor](2),
$$\begin{aligned}
\rho^{GK}_{n,m}\circ(\gamma_{f,R_n}(K_n))_{R_m}
&=f_{R_m}^!(\rho^K_{n,m})\circ\gamma_{f,R_m}((K_n)_{R_m})\\
&=\gamma_{f,R_m}(K_m)\circ f_{R_m}^*(\rho^K_{n,m})(d)[2d].
\end{aligned}$$
All three factors other than $\rho^{GK}_{n,m}$ are isomorphisms by steps 8 and the normalization of $K_\bullet$, so the displayed equation explicitly expresses $\rho^{GK}_{n,m}$ as a composite of isomorphisms. Its common cohomological and Tor bounds are those of $P_\bullet$ via step 8. This proves levelwise constructibility, level-independent cohomological and Tor bounds, and all reduction isomorphisms required by the current definition [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], completing clause (3).

split_report.summary: Repaired the earlier three-step draft into seven steps. The orientation is assembled in the abelian tower heart using the purity compatibility at the coefficient unit and the existing fully faithful single-complex embedding. The tensor map is constructed before testing its levels; normalization includes explicit reduction squares and uniform Tor bounds. No new nodes are needed. Second reading makes the semilinear transition square and its inverse explicit, and verifies uniform source bounds before using the restricted adjunction. Current second reading corrects step 5 to conclude isomorphy in the uniform constructible category for arbitrary input towers; normalization is established separately in steps 6-7. Maintainer reading (2026-10-17) adds det-sp-finite-general-ring to steps 2 and 7: the purity maps of det-sp-reduction-compatibilities are defined through its orientation, and its clauses (2)-(3) identify them with the def-pur-smooth-purity-map maps at index en. Q75 repair of the dedicated 2026-10-17 long-step return: replaced old step 4 by steps 4-7 for finite pullback bounds, elementary twist/shift bounds, etale-origin hypotheses, and the evaluated transpose formula. Each non-elementary claim is an application of the existing cited statement, so no duplicate nodes were created. Reused the existing Mathlib leaf lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single for the heart concentration in step 3. Statement and Lean records unchanged; every proof step is under 2000 characters.
